title: Classification of States: Communication, Recurrence and Periodicity
breadcrumb: Stochastic processes → Markov chains → Classification of States: Communication, Recurrence and Periodicity
engineName: Use state diagrams, first-step equations and exact checks to solve Markov-chain problems.
objectives: Define the relevant Markov-chain quantity and interpret it correctly.
Set up equations using the transition matrix and the correct boundary conditions.
Solve finite-state examples exactly and verify the result.

prereq.name: Linear equations and gcd

traps: Do not confuse first passage with occupancy at a fixed time.
Do not forget that the target has zero remaining hitting time.
A hitting probability must lie in [0,1]; a mean time need not be an integer.
Communication is mutual reachability; a one-way path is insufficient.
A closed class has no outgoing transition.
Period is a gcd, not the smallest return time.
howto: Draw the transition graph first. Mark the target or communicating class, write the relevant definition, and then calculate. Try each scene's question before opening its explanation. Finish by checking the result against the original transition structure.

Every edge on the path must have positive probability.
A direct one-step transition is not required.

scenes.title: A network of communicating states
body: In a directed network, two locations communicate if each can eventually reach the other. A one-way route does not establish communication.
A communicating class is closed if no transition from a state in the class leads outside it.

scenario.teaser: A one-way exit changes the class
scenario.title: A network with an absorbing destination
body: States 1 and 2 reach one another. State 2 can also move to state 3, while state 3 is absorbing. State 3 cannot return to either 1 or 2. Therefore {1,2} is a communicating class but is not closed; {3} is closed.
scenario.answer: The singleton class {3}, because no transition leaves state 3.

ask.q: Why do states 1 and 2 not communicate with state 3?
ask.nudge: Can state 3 reach either of them?

blocks.body: i↔j if i is reachable from j and j is reachable from i.
Every finite closed communicating class is recurrent. In a finite chain, states outside the closed classes are transient. All states in a communicating class share the same period.

scenes.title: Exam summary
scenes.objective: Consolidate communication, closure, recurrence and period.
body: Communication is mutual reachability and partitions the state space into classes.
A class is closed when no transition leaves it. In a finite chain, closed communicating classes are recurrent; states outside them are transient.
Period is gcd{n≥1:pᵢᵢ⁽ⁿ⁾>0}. An absorbing state has period one; an alternating two-state chain has period two.

ask.q: What is the correct order for classifying a finite chain?
ask.nudge: Find classes, test closure, then classify recurrence and period.
